1. Information Gathering Methods

CampusCare is an automated facility maintenance and incident lifecycle resolution system engineered for Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), covering 20 Residential Halls, 84 constituent hostels, and numerous academic faculties. The requirements baseline was established using five empirical methods.

1.1 Method Comparison

MethodHow It Was AppliedStrengthsWeaknessesContribution
Academic Literature ReviewReviewed peer-reviewed papers on smart campus helpdesks and NLP duplicate detection.Formal foundations & validated patterns.Lacks on-ground field realities.4-tier spatial hierarchy, TF-IDF cosine duplicate threshold (≥ 0.55), SLA matrices.
Field Observation of AMU FacilitiesInspected maintenance notebooks in residential halls (Sir Syed Hall, MM Hall, Aftab Hall).Revealed lost registers, handwriting ambiguities, duplicate entries.Restricted to public counters and day shifts.Confirmed >40% duplicate filings in shared hostels; inspired zero-login QR codes.
Stakeholder InterviewsInterviews with 4 Provosts, 6 Wardens, 8 Technicians, 2 Estate Officers, and 15 students.Uncovered technician dispatch fatigue and student mistrust of closures.Small initial sample size.Formulated the 5-minute dwell timer, zero-login task portal, and -15 penalty.
Campus Student SurveysSurvey administered to 180+ AMU resident and day-scholar students.Quantifiable data across demographics.Self-selected tech sample.88.4% preferred zero-account reporting, justifying 32-char hex tokens.
Industry Case StudiesAnalyzed FixMyStreet (civic reporting) and Samarth eGov Suite.Proven municipal scale and spatial mapping.Commercial closed-source constraints.Community upvote mechanism, spatial GPS heatmap, and CSV audit export.

1.2 Most Effective Approach

A hybrid methodology was most effective. Field observations and interviews identified operational realities (zero-login necessity, anti-fraud dwell timers, closed-loop student ratings), while literature reviews provided the mathematical TF-IDF duplicate detection model, and industry benchmarks established civic upvoting and heatmap analytics.

2. Detailed Requirements Specification

2.1 System Overview

2.1.1 Problem Statement

In collegiate universities like AMU, physical maintenance relies on paper registers. This leads to misplaced tickets, duplicate reports in shared rooms, lack of tracking, and unilateral remote closures without repair verification.

2.1.2 Existing System

Manual paper notebooks kept at hall provost or dining offices. Staff manually transcribe slips and verbally assign jobs to technicians without SLA tracking or status verification.

2.1.3 Problems with the Existing Approach

Paper registers are frequently lost, lack spatial details (room/floor/wing), cannot detect duplicate entries, offer zero tracking references to students, and permit fraudulent closures without photo verification.

2.1.4 Proposed System

A centralized web platform utilizing room QR codes, NLP duplicate detection (TF-IDF cosine similarity ≥ 0.55), zero-login technician task execution, a strict 5-minute anti-fraud dwell timer, and closed-loop student rating.

2.1.5 Objectives

• Model campus spatial hierarchy (Campus → Building → Floor → Room) with printable QR codes.
• Provide zero-login complaint filing with private 32-char hex tracking tokens.
• Curb duplicate filings via semantic NLP similarity detection.
• Enforce on-site technician presence via an anti-fraud 5-minute dwell timer and photo proof.
• Implement closed-loop student ratings with automatic disk storage media purging.

2.1.6 Scope

In Scope: Spatial asset modeling, QR code generation, anonymous filing, NLP duplicate triage, automated dispatch, zero-login task portal, 5-minute dwell timer, photo proof, student rating/dispute, dynamic SLAs, and GPS heatmaps.
Out of Scope: Financial procurement of spare parts, payroll, native compiled mobile apps, external contractor bidding.

2.1.7 Target Users

Students & Residents, Field Maintenance Technicians (Electricians, Plumbers, Carpenters), Hall Provosts & Wardens, Department Heads (HODs), and University Registrar / Super Administrators.

2.1.8 Advantages

Reduces filing time to < 60 seconds; eliminates up to 40% duplicate tickets; enforces technician physical presence; gives students closure authority; runs with zero software licensing costs.

2.1.9 Assumptions and Constraints

Assumes students and technicians have smartphones with camera and browser capabilities. Constrained to run on institutional server hardware with in-memory image processing to prevent disk bloat.

2.1.10 User Roles and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

Implements 6 distinct roles: Anonymous Student (QR filing & token tracking), Field Staff (stateless UUID task links), Hall Provost (strictly hall-scoped ORM querysets), Trade HOD (trade-scoped queues), Registrar (global university console), and Estate Officer.

2.2 Functional Requirements

Details FR-001 (Spatial Hierarchy) through FR-015 (Geospatial Heatmap), covering batch QR printing, zero-login reporting, TF-IDF duplicate prompts, automated staff dispatch, 5-minute dwell timer, mandatory photo proof, rating loops, dispute penalties, and dynamic SLAs.

2.2.1 Incident Scope, Visibility & Verification Rules

Public open ticket counts per room encourage upvoting. Ticket details are private to reporters via 32-char hex tokens. Technicians only see dispatched tasks. Hall Provosts have strict row-level scoping preventing cross-hall data leakage. Closures require student ratings or a 72-hour auto-closure window.

2.3 Non-Functional Requirements

• NFR-01 (Performance): Page loads < 800ms, duplicate checks < 150ms, 150+ concurrent users.
• NFR-02 (Security): 128-bit CSPRNG hex tokens, UUIDv4 task links, CSRF protection, in-memory Pillow image sanitization.
• NFR-03 (Usability): Mobile-first responsive layout (min 360px), zero-login simplicity, WCAG 2.1 AA.
• NFR-04 (Reliability): Immutable StatusHistory audit trail, 99.9% uptime target, idempotent state transitions.
• NFR-05 (Maintainability): Modular Django MVT architecture, PEP 8 compliance, 100% test pass rate.

2.4 Data Requirements

2.4.1 Relationships

Campus 1:N Building (self-referential parent hall to constituent hostels), Building 1:N Floor, Floor 1:N Room, Department 1:N Category, Department 1:N UserProfile, Room 1:N Complaint, Complaint 1:N StatusHistory, Complaint 1:N ComplaintUpvote, Complaint 1:1 Feedback.

2.4.2 Indexes

Unique indexes on Complaint.reference_id, Complaint.tracking_token, Complaint.staff_task_token, and Room.qr_code_token. Composite unique index on ComplaintUpvote(complaint_id, session_key). B-Tree indexes on status and created_at.

2.4.3 Database Design Notes

Soft-deletion via is_active on spatial entities. Attached resolution photo files are permanently purged from physical disk storage upon ticket closure to cap long-term storage growth.

2.5 System Requirements

Python 3.9+, Django 5.0+, SQLite/PostgreSQL, Scikit-learn, Pillow, Linux VPS (2 vCPUs, 4GB RAM), Nginx (TLS 1.3), Gunicorn, modern mobile browser with camera.

3.9 Sequence Diagram — Student Scans QR & Submits Complaint

Student camera scans QR code → Web gateway resolves qr_code_token → Pre-fills Room hierarchy → Student enters issue → TF-IDF similarity evaluation → If unique, Complaint created → Returns 32-char tracking token.

3.10 Sequence Diagram — Automated Dispatch & Staff Matching

Ticket creation triggers dispatcher → Queries candidate staff matching trade category → Evaluates hall proximity and lowest active queue → Assigns technician → Generates UUID task token → Dispatches direct task URL.

3.11 Sequence Diagram — Technician Zero-Login Execution & 5-Min Dwell Timer

Technician opens task URL → Taps 'Start Work' → Status becomes IN_PROGRESS & logs timestamp → On-site repair → If resolved in < 5 mins, HTTP 400 rejection with countdown timer → Once ≥ 5 mins, uploads photo proof → Marks RESOLVED.

3.12 Sequence Diagram — Student Searches, Filters & Tracks Complaint

Student visits /track/<tracking_token>/ → System validates 128-bit token entropy → Returns current status, SLA countdown, assigned trade, and progress stepper.

3.13 Sequence Diagram — Closed-Loop Verification, Rating & Media Purge

Student inspects resolution photo → Submits 1-5 star rating → Status becomes CLOSED → purge_attached_media() deletes photo files from physical server disk storage.

3.14 Sequence Diagram — Administrator Manages Users & Roster

Provost logs into /dashboard/ → Queryscoper filters complaints strictly to provost's hall → Provost inspects technician loads → Manually reassigns staff if needed → Audit trail recorded.

3.15 Activity Diagram — Complaint Lodging & Duplicate Detection Workflow

Figure 3.5: Activity Diagram Representing Incident Workflow & Anti-Fraud Gates Procedural flowchart detailing QR scans, duplicate prompt decisions, technician dwell timer checks, and closed-loop verification.

3.16 Activity Diagram — Technician On-Site Repair & Anti-Fraud Dwell Timer

Procedural decision logic: Technician taps Start Work → Physical repair executed → Attempt resolution → Elapsed time check (≥ 5 mins?) → If No, reject & display countdown timer → If Yes, compress photo proof & set Resolved.

3.17 Activity Diagram — Student Verification & Dispute Escalation Workflow

Student inspects proof → Decision: Satisfied? → If Yes: Submit 1-5 stars → Status Closed → Media Purge. If No: Submit dispute reason (≥ 10 chars) & photo → Status In Progress (Priority 95) → Deduct -15 staff score penalty.

3.18 Complaint Lifecycle (State Machine)

Governed by 6 strict operational states: OPEN → ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED (or DISPUTED).

3.20 Authentication and Security

Zero-login unguessable 128-bit CSPRNG hex tokens for students; stateless UUIDv4 links for technicians; PBKDF2 password hashing; row-level ORM filters; in-memory Pillow image sanitization.

3.21 Error Handling and HTTP Status Codes

• 400 Bad Request: Dwell timer rejected (< 5 mins), dispute rationale < 10 chars, unsupported image type.
• 401 Unauthorized: Unauthenticated access to administrative console.
• 403 Forbidden: Cross-tenant query attempt (Provost A querying Hall B data).
• 404 Not Found: Invalid tracking token or task token.
• 429 Too Many Requests: Rate limiting exceeded.
• 500 Internal Server Error: Database exception with graceful heuristic fallback.

3.22 Design Tools and Limitations

Built with VS Code, Git, Django ORM, and Mermaid.js. Trade-offs include deterministic NLP vocabulary boundaries, server clock synchronization dependency for dwell timer, and single-node default storage.

4. Implementation

4.1 Technology Stack Justification

Django 5.0+ MVT for robust built-in security; SQLite/PostgreSQL for 3NF referential integrity; Scikit-learn for offline sub-10ms TF-IDF inference; Pillow for in-memory image compression; Vanilla CSS for fast zero-build styling; Leaflet.js for free GIS heatmaps.

4.2 Interface Design

Room QR landing view pre-populating hall/floor/room badges; submission view with real-time duplicate prompts; private tracking portal with 4-step stepper; technician mobile task portal with live 5-minute countdown clock; scoped administrative consoles.

4.3 Implementation Status

All 15 core functional requirements are implemented and verified in production-ready status.

5. Conclusion and Future Scope

5.1 Future Scope

• Multilingual NLP: Fine-tune IndicBERT for Hindi and Urdu ticket descriptions.
• Predictive Maintenance: Schedule servicing based on historical breakdown frequencies.
• Offline PWA: Enable Service Workers for offline complaint drafting.
• Spare Parts ERP Integration: Automate technician parts requisitions from stores.

5.2 Conclusion

CampusCare transforms facility maintenance at Aligarh Muslim University from an error-prone, manual register process into an automated, transparent, and accountable digital helpdesk. Through room QR codes, zero-login token tracking, NLP duplicate detection, automated dispatch, 5-minute dwell timer enforcement, and closed-loop student ratings, CampusCare establishes a production-ready institutional standard.
